Salem
SAY-lem
n. (the ancient city of Melchizedek, identified with Jerusalem)
Hebrew Shalem (H8004), peace, from shalom, peace, wholeness, completeness.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Salem is the city of the mysterious priest-king who meets Abraham returning victorious from the rescue of Lot: “Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the most high God” (Genesis 14:18). The name means peace, and the psalmist later fixes Salem’s location beyond doubt by pairing it with Israel’s own holy hill: “In Salem also is his tabernacle, and his dwelling place in Zion” (Psalm 76:2) — Salem is Jerusalem under its most ancient recorded name, centuries before David captured it from the Jebusites. The author of Hebrews, expounding Melchizedek’s significance as a type of Christ, draws directly on the name’s meaning: this priest-king met Abraham, blessed him, received tithes from him, and was “first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, which is, King of peace” (Hebrews 7:2). The order is deliberate and doctrinally loaded — righteousness first, then peace, exactly the gospel order in which Christ, the greater Melchizedek, brings peace only on the ground of accomplished righteousness (Romans 5:1). Salem’s brief appearance in Genesis thus becomes, in the hands of the New Testament, a name freighted with the whole logic of the gospel centuries before Sinai.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no separate entry for Salem under this exact heading beyond noting it as Jerusalem's ancient name; the word means peace, and the city is first named as Melchizedek's seat in Genesis 14.

expand to see more

SALEM, n. The ancient name of Jerusalem, meaning peace, first mentioned as the city of Melchizedek.

MELCHIZEDEK, n. The priest-king of Salem who blessed Abraham; a type of Christ's eternal priesthood.

TITHE, n. The tenth part of one's income or produce, set apart as an offering; Abraham's gift to Melchizedek.

TYPE, n. In theology, a person, event, or thing in the Old Testament that prefigures a corresponding reality in the New.

RIGHTEOUSNESS, n. Purity of heart and rectitude of life; conformity to the divine law; in the gospel, imputed through Christ.

Key Scripture

Genesis 14:18 — "And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the most high God."

Psalm 76:2 — "In Salem also is his tabernacle, and his dwelling place in Zion."

Hebrews 7:1 — "For this Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him;"

Hebrews 7:2 — "To whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all; first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, which is, King of peace;"

Modern Corruption

A New Testament writer building an elaborate typological argument on the precise meaning of an obscure Old Testament place-name is not the move of a text inventing doctrine loosely from vague sources.

expand to see more

Historical-critical readings that treat the Melchizedek episode as a late, awkwardly inserted fragment with no real theological weight in its original Genesis context cannot easily explain the New Testament's own confidence in building a load-bearing argument for Christ's priesthood on it (Hebrews 5–7) — a fragile textual accident does not bear that kind of apostolic weight; a genuine, providentially placed anticipation of Christ does.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the gospel order Hebrews draws from the name itself: righteousness before peace, never peace apart from righteousness. Every modern impulse to seek peace — personal, social, ecclesiastical — while setting aside the prior demand of righteousness inverts the very order this ancient name was chosen by the Spirit to teach.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Shalem (H8004), peace; shalom (H7965), peace, wholeness; tsedeq (H6664), righteousness; ma'aser (H4643), tithe, tenth part.

expand to see more

Hebrew Shalem (H8004) — peace; the name of the ancient city itself.

Hebrew shalom (H7965) — peace, wholeness, completeness; the root word behind Salem.

Hebrew tsedeq (H6664) — righteousness; the first half of Melchizedek's own name and title-order.

Hebrew ma'aser (H4643) — tithe, tenth part; what Abraham gave the king of Salem.

Hebrew kohen (H3548) — priest; Melchizedek's office as king of this city.

Usage

"“Melchizedek king of Salem” — the city's first appearance in Scripture."

"“In Salem also is his tabernacle” — the psalmist's identification with Zion."

"“King of Salem, which is, King of peace” — the New Testament's typological reading of the name."
